title: Access arrangements for learning differences
examples: What is the difference between extra time and a reader?
Do I need to ask for these arrangements myself?
Where do I find the official rules for access arrangements?

explain.say: Today we are learning about support in exams.

items: Support helps show what you know

explain.say: One arrangement is getting extra time in the exam.

draw.text: Extra Time: More Time to Answer

explain.say: If you need extra time, you must get it arranged beforehand.

draw.text: Extra Time: Must be arranged early

explain.say: Another support is using a reader during the exam.
A reader helps if reading the questions is difficult for you.
In real life, this is like needing help reading instructions.

faq.q: What is the main difference between extra time and a reader?
faq.a: Extra time gives you more minutes to write your answers. A reader helps you by reading the questions to you.
asks: When do I use a reader?
What does extra time help with?

faq.q: Do I need to ask for these arrangements myself?
faq.a: You usually need official assessment or guidance from a school or educational body to arrange them. They must be documented.
asks: Can I just tell the teacher I need help?

faq.q: Are these arrangements available for all exams?
faq.a: They are available depending on the specific exam board and the reason for the need. Always check the official guidelines.
asks: Does the exam board decide this?

faq.q: What if I forget to arrange something?
faq.a: If you forget to arrange something, you might not be allowed to use it in the exam. Preparation is very important.
asks: Is it okay to ask on the day?

faq.q: Where can I find the official rules for these arrangements?
faq.a: You should look on the official website of the examination board or your school's special educational needs department.

facts: Access arrangements are support measures for students with identified needs.
Extra time means being given more minutes than the standard exam length.
A reader reads the questions aloud, which helps students with reading difficulties.
These arrangements must usually be arranged and approved by an official body.

quiz.say: If you need more time to write down all your answers, which support do you need?
quiz.why: Extra time directly increases the amount of time you have to write your answers.

wrong.0: The room location does not affect the time allowed for the test.
wrong.2: A reader only helps with understanding the words, not with the time you have to write.
wrong.3: Different papers change the content, but do not change the time limit.

quiz.say: If you find it hard to read the questions printed on the paper, what support is most helpful?
quiz.why: A reader speaks the questions out loud, making them easier to understand.

wrong.0: A different paper might have the same reading difficulty.
wrong.1: The room location does not help you hear the questions read aloud.
wrong.3: Extra time helps with writing speed, not with reading the questions.

quiz.say: Which of these arrangements must be arranged and approved by an official body?

options.show: Both extra time and a reader
options.say: Both extra time and a reader

quiz.why: Both types of support require formal assessment and approval to be valid in an exam.

wrong.0: Both are formal accommodations and require documented approval.
wrong.2: A reader also requires formal assessment to ensure the support is appropriate.
wrong.3: Extra time also needs to be formally assessed and approved by the examination board.
